items.title: Primal and infeasibility certificates for basis pursuit denoising
items.statement:
Let $m,n\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$, let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ act by matrix multiplication in the standard finite coordinate bases, with row and column labels $1$ through their dimensions corresponding to library coordinates $0$ through one less, let $y\in\mathbb R^m$, and let $\epsilon\ge0$. Define $g:\mathbb R^m\to\{0,+\infty\}$ by $g(u)=0$ when $\|u-y\|_2\le\epsilon$ and $g(u)=+\infty$ otherwise. For $p\in\mathbb R^m$, define $g^*(p):=\sup_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\{\langle p,u\rangle-g(u)\}$. Then
$$g^*(p)=\langle p,y\rangle+\epsilon\|p\|_2\qquad(p\in\mathbb R^m).$$
Let $A^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$ be the Euclidean adjoint, characterized by $\langle A^*p,z\rangle=\langle p,Az\rangle$ for all $p,z$. If $x\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $\|Ax-y\|_2\le\epsilon$ and a vector $p\in\mathbb R^m$ satisfies $\|A^*p\|_\infty\le1$ and
$$\|x\|_1=-\langle p,y\rangle-\epsilon\|p\|_2,$$
then $x$ minimizes $\|z\|_1$ over that residual ball. If instead $p\ne0$, $A^*p=0$, and $|\langle p,y\rangle|>\epsilon\|p\|_2$, then the residual ball is disjoint from the range of $A$.

references.title: Antonin Chambolle and Thomas Pock, A First-Order Primal-Dual Algorithm for Convex Problems with Applications to Imaging, §2
Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.3

items.axiom_base: No additional axiom; finite-dimensional real algebra only.

items.title: The basis-pursuit denoising objective and residual indicator are proper closed convex
items.statement: Let $m,n\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$, let $y\in\mathbb R^m$, and let $\epsilon\ge0$. Define $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ by $f(x)=\|x\|_1$, and define $g:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ by $g(u)=0$ when $\|u-y\|_2\le\epsilon$ and $g(u)=+\infty$ otherwise. Then $f$ and $g$ are proper (finite somewhere), closed (their epigraphs are closed), and convex (they satisfy the extended-real convex-combination inequality) on their respective finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.

references.title: Antonin Chambolle and Thomas Pock, A First-Order Primal-Dual Algorithm for Convex Problems with Applications to Imaging, §2

items.title: Best s-term ℓ1 approximation error
items.statement:
Let $n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, and let $x\in\mathbb R^n$. Use one-based labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, identifying label $j$ with library coordinate $j-1$. For $T\subseteq[n]$, let $x_{T^c}$ retain the coordinates outside $T$ and vanish on $T$, where $T^c=[n]\setminus T$. Define the best $s$-term $\ell^1$ approximation error by
$$\sigma_s(x)_1:=\min\{\|x_{T^c}\|_1:T\subseteq[n],\ |T|\le s\}.$$
The indexing family is finite and nonempty, so the displayed minimum exists and is attained.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §2.1 Definition 2.2 and §4.3
Shahar Mendelson, Holger Rauhut, and Rachel Ward, Improved Bounds for Sparse Recovery from Subsampled Random Convolutions, §2.1

items.title: The ℓ2 robust nullspace property
items.statement:
Let $m,n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, and let $0<\rho<1$ and $\tau>0$. In real scalar expressions, a natural number denotes its canonical real image. Use one-based coordinate labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, identifying coordinate label $j$ with library coordinate $j-1$. For $h\in\mathbb R^n$ and $S\subseteq[n]$, let $h_S$ agree with $h$ on $S$ and vanish on $S^c=[n]\setminus S$. The matrix $A$ satisfies the **$\ell^2$ robust nullspace property of order $s$ with constants $(\rho,\tau)$** if
$$\|h_S\|_2\le \frac{\rho}{\sqrt{s}}\|h_{S^c}\|_1+\tau\|Ah\|_2$$
for every $h\in\mathbb R^n$ and every $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le s$. This condition applies to all vectors, including vectors with $Ah\ne0$.

references.title: Shahar Mendelson, Holger Rauhut, and Rachel Ward, Improved Bounds for Sparse Recovery from Subsampled Random Convolutions, §2.1 Definition 2.1
Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.3

items.title: A feasible finite-dimensional BPDN problem attains its minimum
items.statement:
Let $m,n\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$, let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ act in the standard finite coordinate bases, with labels $j=1,\ldots,n$ corresponding to library coordinates $j-1$, $y\in\mathbb R^m$, and $\epsilon\ge0$. If
$$F:=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:\|Az-y\|_2\le\epsilon\}$$
is nonempty, then $z\mapsto\|z\|_1$ attains a minimum on $F$.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.3

items.axiom_base: ZF only; finite-dimensional real analysis and exact algebra.

items.title: A block-tail estimate for the largest coordinates
items.statement:
Let $n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, and let $h\in\mathbb R^n$ use one-based coordinate labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with label $j$ corresponding to library coordinate $j-1$. In real scalar expressions, a natural number denotes its canonical real image. Order the coordinates by decreasing $|h_j|$, breaking ties by increasing $j$. Let $S$ consist of the first $s$ indices, and partition $S^c$ in this same order into consecutive nonempty blocks $T_1,\ldots,T_q$ of size $s$, with only the last block possibly smaller; if $S^c=\varnothing$, take $q=0$. Then
$$\|h_{S^c}\|_2\le \|h_S\|_2+\frac{\|h_{S^c}\|_1}{\sqrt{s}}.$$

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.3 proof of Theorem 4.25
Shahar Mendelson, Holger Rauhut, and Rachel Ward, Improved Bounds for Sparse Recovery from Subsampled Random Convolutions, §2.1

items.axiom_base: No additional axiom; finite coordinate ordering and real arithmetic only.

items.title: Certified basis-pursuit denoising by primal-dual hybrid gradient
items.statement:
Inputs are integers $m,n\ge1$, a matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ in the standard finite coordinate bases, a vector $y\in\mathbb R^m$, a radius $\epsilon\ge0$, positive real step sizes $\alpha,\beta$, an initial primal-dual state $x^0\in\mathbb R^n$, $p^0\in\mathbb R^m$, a nonnegative integer sweep cap $N$, positive integer proximal-call caps $C_f,C_{g^*}$, and deterministic finite solver programs with Boolean certificate checkers for the two proximal calls. Each solver/checker record must be complete and well-formed. Admissible solver/checker pairs satisfy the soundness condition that an accepted output is an exact minimizer of its stated proximal subproblem; this is an input assumption, not a finite proof search performed by the procedure.

Set $f(x)=\|x\|_1$ and $g(u)=0$ when $\|u-y\|_2\le\epsilon$, with $g(u)=+\infty$ otherwise. Define the Fenchel conjugate by $g^*(p)=\sup_{u\in\mathbb R^m}(\langle p,u\rangle-g(u))$. For a proper closed convex function $q$ and $t>0$, $\operatorname{prox}_{tq}(v)$ denotes the unique minimizer of $q(w)+\|w-v\|_2^2/(2t)$. Let $A^*$ be the Euclidean adjoint and let $\|A\|_2=\sup_{\|v\|_2\le1}\|Av\|_2$. The target is
$$\min_{z\in\mathbb R^n}\|z\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|Az-y\|_2\le\epsilon.$$

Return **invalid-input** if dimensions or vectors do not match, if $\epsilon<0$, if $N$ is not a nonnegative integer, if either proximal cap is not a positive integer, if either step size is nonpositive, if either solver/checker record is missing or malformed, or if the exact strict check $\alpha\beta\|A\|_2^2<1$ fails. For admissible inputs initialize $\bar x^0=x^0$ and perform the exact primal-dual hybrid-gradient recurrence for at most $N$ sweeps:
$$p^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\beta g^*}(p^k+\beta A\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha f}(x^k-\alpha A^*p^{k+1}),\qquad \bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.$$
Use the supplied solver/checker pairs and caps for the corresponding proximal calls. Propagate any **invalid-input**, **prox-call-failed**, or **prox-cap-exhausted** status and the state returned by the primal-dual procedure. If all $N$ sweeps complete, let $(x,p)$ be the final primal-dual state and perform these exact tests in order:

- If $p\ne0$, $A^*p=0$, and $|\langle p,y\rangle|>\epsilon\|p\|_2$, return **infeasible**.
- Otherwise, if $\|Ax-y\|_2\le\epsilon$, $\|A^*p\|_\infty\le1$, and $\|x\|_1=-\langle p,y\rangle-\epsilon\|p\|_2$, return **success** with $x$.
- If neither certificate passes, return **budget-exhausted** with the final state.

For $N=0$, test the initial state. The certificate tests use exact real comparisons. The procedure makes no guarantee that a finite run finds a certificate and makes no convergence or finite-termination claim.

references.title: Antonin Chambolle and Thomas Pock, A First-Order Primal-Dual Algorithm for Convex Problems with Applications to Imaging, §§2–3.1
Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.3

items.axiom_base: No additional axiom; finite-dimensional real algebra and the explicitly supplied finite proximal solver/checker programs.

items.title: The coordinate-tail and sparse-vector formulations of best s-term error agree
items.statement:
Let $n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, and let $x\in\mathbb R^n$ use the one-based labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with label $j$ corresponding to library coordinate $j-1$. For $T\subseteq[n]$, $x_{T^c}$ agrees with $x$ off $T$ and is zero on $T$. Define $\sigma_s(x)_1:=\min\{\|x_{T^c}\|_1:T\subseteq[n],\ |T|\le s\}$. Define $\operatorname{supp}(z):=\{j\in[n]:z_j\ne0\}$ using the one-based labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with label $j$ corresponding to library coordinate $j-1$. Then
$$\sigma_s(x)_1=\min\{\|x-z\|_1:z\in\mathbb R^n,\ |\operatorname{supp}(z)|\le s\},$$
and this sparse-vector minimum is attained.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §2.1 Definition 2.2
Shahar Mendelson, Holger Rauhut, and Rachel Ward, Improved Bounds for Sparse Recovery from Subsampled Random Convolutions, §2.1

items.axiom_base: No additional axiom; finite coordinate sums and a finite attained minimum.

items.title: The largest coordinates attain the best s-term ℓ1 error
items.statement:
Let $n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, and let $x\in\mathbb R^n$ use the one-based coordinate labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with label $j$ corresponding to library coordinate $j-1$. Order the coordinates by decreasing $|x_j|$, breaking ties by increasing $j$, and let $S$ be the first $s$ indices. For every $U\subseteq[n]$, let $x_U$ agree with $x$ on $U$ and vanish on $U^c$. Then for every $T\subseteq[n]$ with $|T|\le s$,
$$\|x_T\|_1\le\|x_S\|_1\quad\text{and}\quad\|x_{S^c}\|_1\le\|x_{T^c}\|_1.$$
Consequently $\sigma_s(x)_1=\|x_{S^c}\|_1$, so the best $s$-term tail error is attained by retaining the first $s$ coordinates in the specified order.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §2.1 Definition 2.2
Shahar Mendelson, Holger Rauhut, and Rachel Ward, Improved Bounds for Sparse Recovery from Subsampled Random Convolutions, §2.1

items.axiom_base: No additional axiom; finite coordinate ordering only.

items.title: Robust nullspace property gives stable noisy recovery
items.statement:
Let $m,n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$. Use one-based coordinate labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with label $j$ corresponding to library coordinate $j-1$, and interpret natural numbers in real scalar expressions as their canonical real images. Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ and suppose that for some $0<\rho<1$ and $\tau>0$,
$$\|h_S\|_2\le\frac{\rho}{\sqrt{s}}\|h_{S^c}\|_1+\tau\|Ah\|_2$$
for every $h\in\mathbb R^n$ and every $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le s$, where for any vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$, $v_S$ agrees with $v$ on $S$ and vanishes on $S^c=[n]\setminus S$. Let $x^\dagger\in\mathbb R^n$, $\epsilon\ge0$, and $e\in\mathbb R^m$ satisfy $y=Ax^\dagger+e$ and $\|e\|_2\le\epsilon$. Define
$$\sigma_s(x^\dagger)_1:=\min\{\|x^\dagger_{T^c}\|_1:T\subseteq[n],\ |T|\le s\}.$$
The indexing family is finite and nonempty, so this minimum is attained; it also equals the minimum of $\|x^\dagger-z\|_1$ over vectors $z$ with at most $s$ nonzero coordinates. Then the basis-pursuit denoising problem
$$\min_{z\in\mathbb R^n}\|z\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|Az-y\|_2\le\epsilon$$
has a minimizer. Every minimizer $\widehat x$ satisfies
$$\|\widehat x-x^\dagger\|_2\le C_1\frac{\sigma_s(x^\dagger)_1}{\sqrt{s}}+C_2\epsilon,\qquad \|\widehat x-x^\dagger\|_1\le C_3\sigma_s(x^\dagger)_1+C_4\sqrt{s}\,\epsilon,$$
where
$$C_1=\frac{2(1+2\rho)}{1-\rho},\quad C_2=\frac{6\tau}{1-\rho},\quad C_3=\frac{2(1+\rho)}{1-\rho},\quad C_4=\frac{4\tau}{1-\rho}.$$
If the certified finite basis-pursuit denoising procedure returns **success**, its returned vector is a minimizer and satisfies these same bounds. Only reconstruction error is bounded; the theorem asserts neither uniqueness nor support recovery.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.3, Theorem 4.22
Shahar Mendelson, Holger Rauhut, and Rachel Ward, Improved Bounds for Sparse Recovery from Subsampled Random Convolutions, §2.1, Theorem 2.2

items.axiom_base: ZF only; finite-dimensional real algebra and the stated finite-dimensional compactness theorem.

title: Stable compressed sensing with noise — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Bounded noise, compressible truth, and a large nullspace component
items.statement:
In the first two cases take $A=I_2:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$, $s=1$, $\rho=\tfrac12$, and $\tau=1$. This matrix satisfies the robust nullspace property for every vector: for each $S\subseteq\{1,2\}$ with $|S|\le1$, $\|h_S\|_2\le\|h\|_2=\|Ah\|_2$, while the other term on the right side of the robust inequality is nonnegative.

1. **Bounded noise.** Let $x^\dagger=(1,0)$, $e=(0,\tfrac1{10})$, $y=(1,\tfrac1{10})$, and $\epsilon=\tfrac1{10}$. The truth is feasible, the noise bound is attained, and $\sigma_1(x^\dagger)_1=0$. Every minimizer therefore obeys the recovery bounds with $C_1=8$, $C_2=12$, $C_3=6$, and $C_4=8$.

2. **Compressible truth.** Let $x^\dagger=(1,\tfrac15)$, $e=(0,\tfrac1{100})$, $y=(1,\tfrac{21}{100})$, and $\epsilon=\tfrac1{100}$. The truth is feasible and $\sigma_1(x^\dagger)_1=\tfrac15$. Every minimizer obeys the same constants and hence
$$\|\widehat x-x^\dagger\|_2\le\tfrac{43}{25},\qquad \|\widehat x-x^\dagger\|_1\le\tfrac{32}{25}.$$

3. **A large nullspace component outside the theorem's hypothesis.** Let $A_0:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be $A_0(z_1,z_2)=z_1$, take $s=1$, $x^\dagger=(0,M)$ for any $M>0$, $e=0$, $\epsilon=0$, and $y=0$. The only minimum-$\ell^1$ feasible vector is $\widehat x=(0,0)$, so $\|\widehat x-x^\dagger\|_2=M$ while $\sigma_1(x^\dagger)_1=0$. The robust nullspace property fails for $A_0$, witnessed by $h=(0,1)$ and $S=\{2\}$; this case is outside the theorem and shows why its matrix hypothesis cannot be omitted.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.3
Shahar Mendelson, Holger Rauhut, and Rachel Ward, Improved Bounds for Sparse Recovery from Subsampled Random Convolutions, §2.1

items.axiom_base: No additional axiom; exact finite-dimensional real calculations.
